records.source: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר מֹשֶׁ֖ה אֶל־בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל כְּכֹ֛ל אֲשֶׁר־צִוָּ֥ה יְהוָ֖ה אֶת־מֹשֶֽׁה׃פ
records.gloss: And said Moses to [the] sons of Israel according to all that commanded Yahweh Moses.
pieces: So Moses told the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} everything {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had commanded him.

L.1: And Moses spoke to the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel according to all that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had commanded Moses.

R.1: Moses told the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} everything {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had commanded him.

decisions.choice: verse numbers: in many Bibles this verse is 29:40
decisions.reason: This translation numbers verses as the Hebrew text does. In the Hebrew text chapter 29 ends one verse earlier, and this verse, which closes the list of festival offerings, is the first verse of chapter 30. Many Bibles number it 29:40 and so number the rest of this chapter (30:2-17 here) 30:1-16. The words are the same; only the numbers differ.

decisions.choice: all that the LORD commanded: the laws of the set times and their offerings in chapters 28-29
decisions.reason: The verse closes the long instruction that began in 28:1-2, on the daily, Sabbath, monthly and festival offerings. It reports that Moses passed all of it on to the people, just as 29:39 sums it up.

decisions.choice: him
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "him" for the second "Moses", which Hebrew repeats where English would use a pronoun. Literal keeps the name.

records.source: וַיְדַבֵּ֤ר מֹשֶׁה֙ אֶל־רָאשֵׁ֣י הַמַּטּ֔וֹת לִבְנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לֵאמֹ֑ר זֶ֣ה הַדָּבָ֔ר אֲשֶׁ֖ר צִוָּ֥ה יְהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: And spoke Moses to [the] heads of the tribes of [the] sons of Israel, saying, this [is] the word which commanded Yahweh:
pieces: Moses spoke to the heads of the tribes of the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}. He said, "This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has commanded:

L.2: And Moses spoke to the heads of the tribes of the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel, saying, "This [is] the word which {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has commanded:

R.2: Moses spoke to the leaders of the tribes of the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}. He said, "This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has commanded.

decisions.choice: verse numbers: many Bibles begin chapter 30 here
decisions.reason: This translation numbers verses as the Hebrew text does. Many Bibles count the verse before this one as 29:40 and begin chapter 30 here, so 30:2-17 here is 30:1-16 there. The words are the same; only the numbers differ.

decisions.choice: the heads of the tribes: the leaders of each tribe
decisions.reason: These are the men at the head of the tribes and their families (1:4, 16; 7:2). The law that follows is given to them first because it deals with the authority of fathers and husbands within the household, which the heads of families and tribes would uphold.

decisions.choice: the word: the matter or instruction
decisions.reason: The noun means "word" and also "thing, matter". With "which the LORD commanded" it introduces a command, as in Exodus 16:16 and Leviticus 8:5; 17:2.

decisions.choice: leaders
decisions.reason: Readable says "leaders" for "heads", the plain sense of the word here.

records.heading: Vows and pledges

records.source: אִישׁ֩ כִּֽי־יִדֹּ֨ר נֶ֜דֶר לַֽיהוָ֗ה אֽוֹ־הִשָּׁ֤בַע שְׁבֻעָה֙ לֶאְסֹ֤ר אִסָּר֙ עַל־נַפְשׁ֔וֹ לֹ֥א יַחֵ֖ל דְּבָר֑וֹ כְּכָל־הַיֹּצֵ֥א מִפִּ֖יו יַעֲשֶֽׂה׃
records.gloss: A man, when he vows a vow to Yahweh or swears an oath to bind a bond on himself, not he shall profane his word; according to all the [thing] going out from his mouth he shall do.
pieces: When a man makes a vow to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} or swears an oath that binds him to a pledge, he must not break his word. He must do everything he has said.

L.3: A man, when he vows a vow to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} or swears an oath to bind a bond on himself, he shall not profane his word; according to all that goes out of his mouth he shall do.

R.3: If a man makes a vow to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, or swears an oath that binds him to do something or not do something, he must not break his word. He must do everything he said he would do.

decisions.choice: a vow; an oath to bind a bond: a promise to give or do something, and a sworn pledge that binds the one who makes it
alternatives: a vow to do something and a pledge to refrain from something (reading the two terms as two distinct kinds)
decisions.reason: A vow was a promise made to the LORD to give or do something, often in return for help asked of him (Genesis 28:20-22; 1 Samuel 1:11). The second phrase uses a word built on the verb "to bind": a pledge sworn with an oath that ties the person to a course of action, often to hold back from something (verse 14). The chapter keeps both kinds together and treats them alike.

decisions.choice: a man: a male who makes a vow
decisions.reason: Here the word means a man as against a woman, as verse 4 shows by turning to "a woman". A man's vow stands on his word alone; the rest of the chapter deals with women whose vows a father or husband may cancel.

decisions.choice: not profane his word: not treat his word as empty by failing to keep it
decisions.reason: The verb means to make common or to profane. A promise made to the LORD is holy; to leave it undone treats it as worthless. Deuteronomy 23:22-24 and Ecclesiastes 5:3-4 give the same warning about vows.

decisions.choice: on his soul: on himself
decisions.reason: The word often translated "soul" here means the person himself, his own life. The same phrase recurs through the chapter for the woman who binds herself.

decisions.choice: on himself
decisions.reason: Literal says "on himself" rather than "on his soul", since in English "soul" suggests the inner spirit, not the whole person meant here; the literal gloss shows the Hebrew form.

decisions.choice: binds him to do something or not do something
decisions.reason: Readable spells out what a binding pledge is: a sworn promise to do or to refrain from something.

records.source: וְאִשָּׁ֕ה כִּֽי־תִדֹּ֥ר נֶ֖דֶר לַיהוָ֑ה וְאָסְרָ֥ה אִסָּ֛ר בְּבֵ֥ית אָבִ֖יהָ בִּנְעֻרֶֽיהָ׃
records.gloss: And a woman, when she vows a vow to Yahweh and binds a bond in [the] house of her father in her youth,
pieces: When a woman makes a vow to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} or binds herself by a pledge while she is young and still living in her father's house,

L.4: And a woman, when she vows a vow to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and binds a bond in the house of her father in her youth,

R.4: Suppose a young woman still living in her father's house makes a vow to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} or promises to do or not do something.

decisions.choice: in her father's house in her youth: a young unmarried woman living under her father's authority
decisions.reason: The phrase describes a daughter not yet married, who belongs to her father's household. Her vows could commit the household's goods or her own future, so the law gives her father a say over them (verses 5-6).

decisions.choice: and binds: or binds
decisions.reason: The joining word usually means "and", but here it links two kinds of promise, either of which the law covers, as the "or" of verse 3 does.

decisions.choice: while she is young and still living in her father's house
decisions.reason: Balanced puts her age before the place, which reads more naturally, and adds "still" to show that she has not yet married.

decisions.choice: Suppose a young woman ... makes a vow
decisions.reason: Readable makes the condition a sentence of its own and brings her youth and home to the front, so the next sentence can state what follows.

records.source: וְשָׁמַ֨ע אָבִ֜יהָ אֶת־נִדְרָ֗הּ וֶֽאֱסָרָהּ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר אָֽסְרָ֣ה עַל־נַפְשָׁ֔הּ וְהֶחֱרִ֥ישׁ לָ֖הּ אָבִ֑יהָ וְקָ֨מוּ֙ כָּל־נְדָרֶ֔יהָ וְכָל־אִסָּ֛ר אֲשֶׁר־אָסְרָ֥ה עַל־נַפְשָׁ֖הּ יָקֽוּם׃
records.gloss: and hears her father her vow and her bond which she bound on herself, and keeps silent to her her father, and stand all her vows, and every bond which she bound on herself shall stand.
pieces: and her father hears of her vow or her pledge and says nothing to her, then all her vows stand, and every pledge by which she has bound herself stands.

L.5: and her father hears her vow and her bond which she has bound on herself, and her father keeps silent toward her, then all her vows shall stand, and every bond which she has bound on herself shall stand.

R.5: Her father may hear about her vow or her promise and say nothing to her. Then she must keep all her vows and every promise she has made.

decisions.choice: stand: remain in force
decisions.reason: "Stand" is said of a vow that remains valid and must be kept, as against one that "does not stand" (verse 6). The same verb in its causative form, "make stand", is used in verses 14-15 for a husband who confirms a vow.

decisions.choice: keeps silent: says nothing, and so lets the vow stand
decisions.reason: The father's silence counts as consent. He does not need to approve the vow out loud; if he raises no objection, it holds.

decisions.choice: she must keep
decisions.reason: Readable says what it means for a vow to stand: she is bound to keep it.

records.source: וְאִם־הֵנִ֨יא אָבִ֣יהָ אֹתָהּ֮ בְּי֣וֹם שָׁמְעוֹ֒ כָּל־נְדָרֶ֗יהָ וֶֽאֱסָרֶ֛יהָ אֲשֶׁר־אָסְרָ֥ה עַל־נַפְשָׁ֖הּ לֹ֣א יָק֑וּם וַֽיהוָה֙ יִֽסְלַח־לָ֔הּ כִּי־הֵנִ֥יא אָבִ֖יהָ אֹתָֽהּ׃
records.gloss: But if forbids her father her on [the] day of his hearing, all her vows and her bonds which she bound on herself not shall stand, and Yahweh will forgive her, because forbade her father her.
pieces: But if her father forbids her on the day he hears of it, none of her vows or pledges by which she has bound herself will stand. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} will forgive her, because her father has forbidden her.

L.6: But if her father forbids her on the day he hears, all her vows and her bonds which she has bound on herself shall not stand, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will forgive her, because her father forbade her.

R.6: But her father may tell her no on the day he hears about it. Then none of her vows or promises count. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} will forgive her for not keeping them, because her father stopped her.

decisions.choice: forbids: opposes, holds her back
decisions.reason: The verb means to restrain or hold back, and it is used of discouraging the people from going into the land (32:7, 9). Here it means the father objects to the vow and so stops it.

decisions.choice: on the day he hears: at once, not later
decisions.reason: The father must object on the day he learns of the vow. If he lets that day pass in silence, the vow stands (verse 5; compare verse 15).

decisions.choice: the LORD will forgive her: he will not hold her guilty for leaving the vow unkept
decisions.reason: A broken vow was a sin before God (Deuteronomy 23:22). Because the vow was cancelled by the one with authority over her, the LORD releases her from it and counts no guilt against her.

decisions.choice: for not keeping them
decisions.reason: Readable says what she is forgiven for, which Literal and Balanced leave implied.

records.source: וְאִם־הָי֤וֹ תִֽהְיֶה֙ לְאִ֔ישׁ וּנְדָרֶ֖יהָ עָלֶ֑יהָ א֚וֹ מִבְטָ֣א שְׂפָתֶ֔יהָ אֲשֶׁ֥ר אָסְרָ֖ה עַל־נַפְשָֽׁהּ׃
records.gloss: And if indeed she is to a husband, and her vows [are] on her, or [the] rash utterance of her lips which she bound on herself,
pieces: If she marries while she is still under her vows, or under a rash promise of her lips by which she has bound herself,

L.7: And if she indeed becomes [wife] to a husband while her vows [are] on her, or the rash utterance of her lips by which she has bound herself,

R.7: Suppose a woman gets married while she still has to keep a vow, or a promise she made without thinking.

decisions.choice: if she indeed becomes a husband's: if she marries
alternatives: if she is married (any wife, so that verses 11-13 repeat the case)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "to be to a man" is a common way to say that a woman marries (Ruth 1:12-13; Ezekiel 16:8). The doubled verb stresses the condition. The case is a woman who comes into marriage still bound by vows made before, perhaps in her father's house; verses 11-13 deal with vows made after she is married.

decisions.choice: the rash utterance of her lips: a promise spoken without thought
decisions.reason: The word comes from a verb meaning to speak rashly or thoughtlessly, used in Leviticus 5:4 of a careless oath and in Psalm 106:33 of Moses' words at Meribah. The law allows that a vow may have been spoken in haste.

decisions.choice: becomes [wife] to a husband
decisions.reason: Literal supplies "wife" so the Hebrew phrase can be followed; Balanced and Readable say "marries".

decisions.choice: a promise she made without thinking
decisions.reason: Readable puts "rash utterance" in plain words.

records.source: וְשָׁמַ֥ע אִישָׁ֛הּ בְּי֥וֹם שָׁמְע֖וֹ וְהֶחֱרִ֣ישׁ לָ֑הּ וְקָ֣מוּ נְדָרֶ֗יהָ וֶֽאֱסָרֶ֛הָ אֲשֶׁר־אָסְרָ֥ה עַל־נַפְשָׁ֖הּ יָקֻֽמוּ׃
records.gloss: and hears her husband on [the] day of his hearing and keeps silent to her, and stand her vows, and her bonds which she bound on herself shall stand.
pieces: and her husband hears of it and says nothing to her on the day he hears, then her vows stand, and the pledges by which she has bound herself stand.

L.8: and her husband hears [it] on the day he hears and keeps silent toward her, then her vows shall stand, and her bonds which she has bound on herself shall stand.

R.8: Her husband may hear about it and say nothing to her that day. Then she must keep her vows and the promises she has made.

decisions.choice: on the day he hears: his silence that day lets the vow stand
decisions.reason: As with the father in verse 5, the husband's silence on the day he learns of the vow counts as consent. The rule now passes from father to husband: the one who heads her household has the say.

decisions.choice: she must keep
decisions.reason: As in verse 5.

records.source: וְ֠אִם בְּי֨וֹם שְׁמֹ֣עַ אִישָׁהּ֮ יָנִ֣יא אוֹתָהּ֒ וְהֵפֵ֗ר אֶת־נִדְרָהּ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָלֶ֔יהָ וְאֵת֙ מִבְטָ֣א שְׂפָתֶ֔יהָ אֲשֶׁ֥ר אָסְרָ֖ה עַל־נַפְשָׁ֑הּ וַיהוָ֖ה יִֽסְלַֽח־לָֽהּ׃
records.gloss: But if on [the] day of hearing [of] her husband he forbids her, and he annuls her vow which [is] on her and [the] rash utterance of her lips which she bound on herself, and Yahweh will forgive her.
pieces: But if her husband forbids her on the day he hears of it, he cancels the vow she is under and the rash promise of her lips by which she has bound herself, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will forgive her.

L.9: But if on the day her husband hears [it] he forbids her, then he annuls her vow which [is] on her and the rash utterance of her lips by which she has bound herself, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will forgive her.

R.9: But her husband may tell her no on the day he hears about it. Then he cancels her vow and the promise she made without thinking. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} will forgive her for not keeping it.

decisions.choice: annuls: makes void, cancels
decisions.reason: The verb means to break or make void; it is used of breaking a covenant (Genesis 17:14; Leviticus 26:44) and of bringing plans to nothing (Psalm 33:10). Here the husband's objection undoes the vow so that it no longer binds her.

decisions.choice: the LORD will forgive her
decisions.reason: As in verse 6: the LORD does not count the unkept vow against her.

decisions.choice: cancels
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "cancels", the everyday word; Literal keeps the more formal "annuls" through the chapter.

records.source: וְנֵ֥דֶר אַלְמָנָ֖ה וּגְרוּשָׁ֑ה כֹּ֛ל אֲשֶׁר־אָסְרָ֥ה עַל־נַפְשָׁ֖הּ יָק֥וּם עָלֶֽיהָ׃
records.gloss: And [the] vow of a widow and a divorced [woman], all that she bound on herself shall stand on her.
pieces: But any vow of a widow or a divorced woman, anything by which she has bound herself, is binding on her.

L.10: And the vow of a widow or of a divorced woman, all that she has bound on herself shall stand against her.

R.10: But a widow or a divorced woman must keep every vow and every promise she makes.

decisions.choice: a widow or a divorced woman: a woman with no father or husband over her household
decisions.reason: A widow or a divorced woman was head of her own affairs; no man had authority to cancel her vows, so she answers for them herself, as a man does (verse 3). Leviticus 22:13 speaks of a widowed or divorced priest's daughter who returns to her father's house.

decisions.choice: shall stand on her: is binding on her
decisions.reason: As in verse 5, "stand" means the vow remains in force; "on her" means she is the one who must keep it.

decisions.choice: against her
decisions.reason: Literal says "against her" for "on her", the sense of a duty laid on her; Balanced says "binding on her".

records.source: וְאִם־בֵּ֥ית אִישָׁ֖הּ נָדָ֑רָה אֽוֹ־אָסְרָ֥ה אִסָּ֛ר עַל־נַפְשָׁ֖הּ בִּשְׁבֻעָֽה׃
records.gloss: And if [in the] house of her husband she vowed or bound a bond on herself with an oath,
pieces: If a woman living in her husband's house makes a vow or binds herself by a pledge with an oath,

L.11: And if she vowed in the house of her husband, or bound a bond on herself with an oath,

R.11: Suppose a married woman makes a vow, or swears an oath to do or not do something.

decisions.choice: in her husband's house: after she is married
decisions.reason: This case is a vow made by a wife while living in her husband's household, as against one she brought into the marriage (verse 7). The same rules apply.

decisions.choice: she vowed: past tense, a vow already made
decisions.reason: The verbs look back on a vow already spoken, which the husband then hears of (verse 12).

decisions.choice: to do or not do something
decisions.reason: As in verse 3, Readable spells out what a binding pledge is.

records.source: וְשָׁמַ֤ע אִישָׁהּ֙ וְהֶחֱרִ֣שׁ לָ֔הּ לֹ֥א הֵנִ֖יא אֹתָ֑הּ וְקָ֨מוּ֙ כָּל־נְדָרֶ֔יהָ וְכָל־אִסָּ֛ר אֲשֶׁר־אָסְרָ֥ה עַל־נַפְשָׁ֖הּ יָקֽוּם׃
records.gloss: and heard her husband and kept silent to her, not he forbade her, and stand all her vows, and every bond which she bound on herself shall stand.
pieces: and her husband hears of it and says nothing to her and does not forbid her, then all her vows stand, and every pledge by which she has bound herself stands.

L.12: and her husband heard [it] and kept silent toward her [and] did not forbid her, then all her vows shall stand, and every bond which she has bound on herself shall stand.

R.12: If her husband hears about it and says nothing to her, and does not tell her no, then she must keep all her vows and every promise she has made.

decisions.choice: kept silent, did not forbid her: two ways of saying he raised no objection
decisions.reason: The second phrase restates the first. A husband who hears of the vow and does not object lets it stand, as the father does in verse 5.

decisions.choice: hears ... says nothing
decisions.reason: Balanced puts the case in the present, as the other cases in the chapter are put; Literal keeps the Hebrew past forms that follow on from verse 11.

records.source: וְאִם־הָפֵר֩ יָפֵ֨ר אֹתָ֥ם׀אִישָׁהּ֮ בְּי֣וֹם שָׁמְעוֹ֒ כָּל־מוֹצָ֨א שְׂפָתֶ֧יהָ לִנְדָרֶ֛יהָ וּלְאִסַּ֥ר נַפְשָׁ֖הּ לֹ֣א יָק֑וּם אִישָׁ֣הּ הֲפֵרָ֔ם וַיהוָ֖ה יִֽסְלַֽח־לָֽהּ׃
records.gloss: But if indeed he annuls them, her husband, on [the] day of his hearing, all [that] goes out of her lips concerning her vows and concerning [the] bond of herself not shall stand; her husband annulled them, and Yahweh will forgive her.
pieces: But if her husband cancels them on the day he hears of them, then nothing that came from her lips, whether vows or pledges binding her, will stand. Her husband has cancelled them, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will forgive her.

L.13: But if her husband indeed annuls them on the day he hears, everything that goes out of her lips concerning her vows or concerning the bond on herself shall not stand; her husband has annulled them, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will forgive her.

R.13: But her husband may cancel them on the day he hears about them. Then nothing she said in her vows or promises counts. Her husband has cancelled them, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will forgive her for not keeping them.

decisions.choice: indeed annuls: the doubled verb stresses a clear act
decisions.reason: The verb is repeated, a common Hebrew way of stressing it. The cancellation must be a definite act, not mere silence.

decisions.choice: what goes out of her lips: whatever she has said
decisions.reason: The phrase means the words she has spoken, as "what goes out of his mouth" in verse 3.

decisions.choice: the LORD will forgive her
decisions.reason: As in verse 6: the LORD does not count the unkept vow against her.

decisions.choice: cancels
decisions.reason: As in verse 9.

records.source: כָּל־נֵ֛דֶר וְכָל־שְׁבֻעַ֥ת אִסָּ֖ר לְעַנֹּ֣ת נָ֑פֶשׁ אִישָׁ֥הּ יְקִימֶ֖נּוּ וְאִישָׁ֥הּ יְפֵרֶֽנּוּ׃
records.gloss: Every vow and every oath of bond to afflict [the] soul, her husband shall confirm it, and her husband shall annul it.
pieces: Any vow or any sworn pledge to deny herself, her husband may confirm or her husband may cancel.

L.14: Every vow and every binding oath to afflict [her] soul, her husband may confirm it, and her husband may annul it.

R.14: Her husband may approve or cancel any vow or oath she makes to go without food or other things.

decisions.choice: to afflict the soul: to deny oneself, as by fasting
decisions.reason: The phrase is used for the self-denial of the Day of Atonement (Leviticus 16:29, 31; 23:27, 32; Numbers 29:7) and for fasting (Psalm 35:13; Isaiah 58:3, 5). A vow of this kind would hold her back from food or other ordinary things for a time, which touched the life of the whole household.

decisions.choice: every vow and every binding oath to afflict the soul: both kinds of promise, where they involve self-denial
alternatives: every vow, and every binding oath to afflict the soul (the phrase limited to the oath)
decisions.reason: The phrase "to afflict the soul" may belong to both vow and oath or only to the oath. Either way, the verse names a case where a husband's say over his wife's promises matters most, and the next verses show he may confirm or cancel any of her vows.

decisions.choice: confirm it, annul it: let it stand or cancel it
decisions.reason: "Confirm" is the causative of "stand" (verse 5): he makes the vow stand. The two verbs set out the husband's choice, which verses 15-16 explain.

decisions.choice: afflict [her] soul
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew phrase, with "her" in brackets; Balanced says "deny herself" and Readable "go without food or other things".

decisions.choice: to go without food or other things
decisions.reason: Readable names fasting, the most common form of this self-denial, and adds "or other things" since the vow need not be about food.

records.source: וְאִם־הַחֲרֵשׁ֩ יַחֲרִ֨ישׁ לָ֥הּ אִישָׁהּ֮ מִיּ֣וֹם אֶל־יוֹם֒ וְהֵקִים֙ אֶת־כָּל־נְדָרֶ֔יהָ א֥וֹ אֶת־כָּל־אֱסָרֶ֖יהָ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָלֶ֑יהָ הֵקִ֣ים אֹתָ֔ם כִּי־הֶחֱרִ֥שׁ לָ֖הּ בְּי֥וֹם שָׁמְעֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: But if indeed he keeps silent to her, her husband, from day to day, and he confirms all her vows or all her bonds which [are] on her; he confirmed them, because he kept silent to her on [the] day of his hearing.
pieces: But if her husband says nothing to her from one day to the next, he confirms all her vows and all the pledges she is under. He has confirmed them, because he said nothing to her on the day he heard of them.

L.15: But if her husband indeed keeps silent toward her from day to day, then he confirms all her vows or all her bonds which [are] on her; he has confirmed them, because he kept silent toward her on the day he heard.

R.15: If her husband says nothing to her about it from one day to the next, then he approves all her vows and promises. He has approved them, because he said nothing on the day he heard about them.

decisions.choice: from day to day: past the day he heard, into the next
decisions.reason: The phrase means that a day goes by and another begins without his objecting. Once the day of hearing has passed in silence, the vow is confirmed (verses 8, 12).

decisions.choice: indeed keeps silent: the doubled verb stresses his silence
decisions.reason: As with "indeed annuls" in verse 13, the verb is repeated for stress: silence is itself a decision, and it lets the vow stand.

decisions.choice: and
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "vows and pledges": the Hebrew "or" here lists the kinds of promise, all of which are confirmed.

records.source: וְאִם־הָפֵ֥ר יָפֵ֛ר אֹתָ֖ם אַחֲרֵ֣י שָׁמְע֑וֹ וְנָשָׂ֖א אֶת־עֲוֺנָֽהּ׃
records.gloss: But if indeed he annuls them after his hearing, and he shall bear her guilt.
pieces: But if he cancels them later, after the day he heard of them, he will bear the guilt that would have been hers."

L.16: But if he indeed annuls them after he has heard, then he shall bear her guilt."

R.16: But if he waits and cancels them later, he will be the one held guilty for her broken vows, not she."

decisions.choice: after his hearing: later than the day he heard
decisions.reason: Read with verse 15, "after" means after the day of hearing has passed. By then his silence has confirmed the vow, so a later cancellation comes too late to free her.

decisions.choice: bear her guilt: carry the blame and its penalty in her place
decisions.reason: To "bear guilt" is to be held answerable for a wrong and to carry its consequences (Leviticus 5:1, 17; 19:8). The vow is broken, but the blame falls on the husband who wrongly stopped her, not on the wife.

decisions.choice: later, after the day he heard
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable state what verse 15 implies: "after" means after the day of hearing has passed.

decisions.choice: not she
decisions.reason: Readable says outright that she is not held guilty, which "her guilt" carried by him implies.

records.source: אֵ֣לֶּה הַֽחֻקִּ֗ים אֲשֶׁ֨ר צִוָּ֤ה יְהוָה֙ אֶת־מֹשֶׁ֔ה בֵּ֥ין אִ֖ישׁ לְאִשְׁתּ֑וֹ בֵּֽין־אָ֣ב לְבִתּ֔וֹ בִּנְעֻרֶ֖יהָ בֵּ֥ית אָבִֽיהָ׃פ
records.gloss: These [are] the statutes which commanded Yahweh Moses between a man and his wife, between a father and his daughter in her youth [in the] house of her father.
pieces: These are the statutes that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} commanded Moses about a man and his wife, and about a father and his daughter while she is young and living in her father's house.

L.17: These [are] the statutes which {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} commanded Moses, between a man and his wife, between a father and his daughter in her youth in the house of her father.

R.17: These are the laws {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gave Moses about husbands and wives, and about fathers and their young daughters who still live at home.

decisions.choice: these are the statutes: a closing summary
decisions.reason: The chapter ends with a summary line, as many laws do (Leviticus 7:37-38; 11:46-47; 15:32-33; 27:34). It names the two relationships the law has dealt with; the widow and divorced woman of verse 10 stand outside them.

decisions.choice: between a man and his wife: concerning the bond between them
decisions.reason: "Between" here means the matters that concern the two of them, in particular his say over her vows. "Man" in this phrase means husband.

decisions.choice: about
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "about" for "between", which is what the Hebrew means here.

decisions.choice: laws
decisions.reason: Readable says "laws" for "statutes", as elsewhere in the books of the law.
